fit: injected allspice leaf extract and rat CNS suppression
assessment: Fresh leaf extracts injected in rats decreased general CNS activity. The 14-day oral fraction experiment measured pressure, heart rate and weight. Neither reported depressive behavior or ground allspice berries.

fit: rat CNS activity and fresh allspice leaf extracts
assessment: Rat behavioral screening after injection included nonspecific CNS suppression. No explicit attention task or oral ground-berry comparison was reported.

fit: commercial watermelon juice and supine blood pressure
assessment: Ten young adults in a crossover. Two-hour estimate -13.1 mm Hg (95% CI -24.09 to -2.11, p=.02); the overall interaction was p=.91. No measured lightheadedness or postural test.

fit: pea proteins among several active ingredients and gait within SPPB
assessment: Completed prototype powder trial with separate ingredients and no posted results. Does not test whole cooked peas or Parkinson gait.

fit: pea protein in a mixed sachet and registered walking speed
assessment: Plant blend, whey and control sarcopenia protocol specifies six-meter walking speed. No posted results or sample taking cooked peas alone.

fit: pea beverage and registered walking tasks after resistance exercise
assessment: Three beverages combined with exercise and timed gait assessments in older adults. Recruiting and no posted results. No cooked-pea Parkinson comparison.

fit: nigella-derived melanin and registered reflux endpoints
assessment: Registry specifies GERD-Q and general safety, without a distinct dysphagia measure or whole-ground seed assignment. No posted results.

fit: blend containing marjoram and PSQI in rheumatoid arthritis
assessment: Massage trial reports global sleep changes across groups and no separate REM dream enactment. Mixed essential oils, skin exposure and rheumatoid arthritis differ from the claim.

fit: marjoram massage and bruxism trial or conference abstract
assessment: Registry specifies complaints and bruxism measures. The conference abstract reports jaw ultrasound results. No fresh culinary exposure or dream-enactment measure.

fit: blend containing marjoram, inhalation and topical bruxism trial
assessment: Trial specifies jaw ultrasound with pain and stress symptoms. It does not measure dream enactment and has no posted results.

fit: lipidated curcumin, PSQI daytime dysfunction and older adults
assessment: Table S12 shows 1/38 versus 9/38 worsened at week 12 and 1/38 versus 2/38 improved, with p=.018 for the full category comparison. Daytime dysfunction is a combined component and no separate Epworth or item result was identified.

fit: turmeric-extract combination and registered PSQI daytime dysfunction
assessment: Biomarker-selected chronic pain intervention combines turmeric, black pepper, ashwagandha and olive-leaf extracts. Registry adds no observed daytime functioning or sleepiness data.
Ground cardamom provocation caused hives and gastric symptoms in one allergy case. The article gives no dysphagia during this provocation or chronic Parkinson comparison.

fit: cardamom odor and saliva weight in healthy participants
assessment: Cardamom odor gives a greater saliva weight than rest. The experiment does not test ground cardamom ingestion or measure a swallowing change.

fit: Mediterranean diet adherence and apathy outside Parkinson disease
assessment: Table 4 adjusted OR 2.76, 95% CI 0.83 to 9.21, p=.099 for diet nonadherence and apathy during quarantine. The prose describes an association. There is no oil-specific contrast.

fit: apathy during sublingual cannabinoid treatment with olive oil carrier
assessment: Apathy decreased in one uncontrolled Alzheimer cohort. Same cohort as the 2022 preprint. Formulation uses unspecified olive oil as carrier and there is no carrier-only arm.

fit: multicomponent Parkinson diet and baseline apathy
assessment: Published material includes a baseline Starkstein Apathy Scale and no isolated refined-olive-oil or follow-up apathy contrast.

fit: Parkinson cohort diet scores and individual apathy assessment
assessment: Recovered institutional Table 4 covers 162 participants and MDS-UPDRS I item 1.5. Lifestyle-adjusted MIND, DII and HDI p=.612, .687 and .369. The models use entire dietary patterns and supply no separate oil-grade result.

fit: Parkinson dietary patterns, olive oil questionnaire and patient-rated motivation
assessment: The two diet scores show lower difficulty on the motivation or initiative item at p<.001 each. The supplements list olive oil questions but report question-level estimates only against the aggregate PRO-PD measure. The food processing grade and separate oil-to-apathy estimate are absent.
